items.title: Dalton Richards Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: And Albert Frenchy, who was in with Celestan, and when Papa would have two jobs the same night that he couldn't fulfill, well, he'd get a very good Dixieland trumpet player, like Alvin Alcorn or somebody, and, or another trombone player we call, Showboyd.

ctx.x: Yeah, probably he did. He played a lot of the bands. I know Lee Collins told me he used to be, you know, George Lewis, he learned a lot of things. Yeah, yeah. It was interesting to him, too.

Well, uh, he's an older man in Georgia. Yeah, he was before him. Uh-huh. So, uh, we started playing nightclubs. And I enjoyed it. And Albert Frenchy, who was in with Celestan, and when Papa would have two jobs the same night that he couldn't fulfill, well, he'd get a very good Dixieland trumpet player, like Alvin Alcorn or somebody, and, or another trombone player we call, Showboyd.
I can't think of Showboyd's name, but he was a good... I can't think of it, Alvin.
